obligations.note: The diff changes Retention.isPurgeDue so a legal hold no longer blocks purge when the case status is WITHDRAWN. Withdrawn cases on legal hold will have their NPI purged, which breaks 'never while a legal hold applies'.
The register has no exception for RET-1 / mortgage.retention. The deviation from RET-1 is therefore not covered by any approved, unexpired exception with a compensating control.
Ticket CHG-26761 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-05, before the change opened. Its component mortgage.retention covers the only touched path, Retention.java.
The code_review approval is from Declan Farrell, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage. He is a different person from the author, Nneka Okafor.
The approval names the head commit 3756266, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims a ci-runner-06 run on head starting 2026-10-08. The attached JUnit reports are timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-13, and come from host dev-laptop-7.local, so they are not valid evidence from this CI run. Also, the hold tests (sampledPurgeRespectsHold, retentionPurgeSkipsCasesOnLegalHold) reportedly pass despite the behaviour change, and no test files were changed although the description says unit tests were updated.
The only touched component, mortgage.retention, is not security_sensitive, so no security review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket is standard and the change is not an emergency, so no PIR is due.
No ledger entry covers Retention.java or the RET-1 scope, so this change lapses no prior evidence.

summary: The change exempts withdrawn cases from the legal-hold check, so their NPI can be purged while a legal hold applies. That directly violates RET-1, and no exception covers it. The test evidence is also invalid: the JUnit reports are dated after the review time and come from a developer workstation rather than the recorded CI runner. Ticket and approval records are otherwise in order, but the change must be rejected.
